From: J. Rivera <jriv@nimble-retail.com>

Cc: ops@nimble-retail.com, procurement@nimble-retail.com

Subject: Re: Checkout errors 500/latency spikes - urgent

Laura —

We're seeing a sharp increase in checkout failures starting ~09:50 PT. 5xx rate jumped to 7.8% and P95 latency is at 3.2s (normally ~420ms). This is causing a measurable drop in conversions on the site. Our ops team attached a short CSV with the SLO breach windows and sampling.

Quick context: today is a marketing flash sale (expected traffic 3x baseline). We had traffic shaping in place but the errors are affecting all regions. Can you confirm whether this is related to the model rollout you announced last week or a capacity regression?

We need an ETA for a mitigation and we will need an exec update for our CEO — they're asking for a remediation timeline.

Attachments: nimble_slo_report.csv (CSV, 48KB)

— Javier
CRO, Nimble Retail

From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Checkout errors 500/latency spikes - immediate coordination

Laurel — (cc: team) quick triage notes:

- Initial telemetry shows a correlated increase in KV miss rate and a small regression in batch packing efficiency since the 03:00 deploy of the kernel selector heuristics. GPU utilization climbed to 98% on a subset of hosts running the A100-80GB pool.
- Error signatures indicate transient OOM in the runtime on long-context requests (checkout instructions + cart metadata). Those requests are at ~1.2k tokens in the worst samples.

Immediate plan:
1) Pause the kernel selector rollout on affected nodes and trigger an emergency rebind to the previous kernel set (rollback initiated).
2) Force route large-context checkouts to the quantized 1.2.4 variant (less memory pressure) for the next 60 min.
3) Add short TTL prefix caching for cart-rewrite prompts to reduce repeated long-context evaluation.

I initiated a manual drain of the affected hosts and requested a temporary +2 GPU burst from infra (authorization pending). If we can get the burst, the system should stabilize within ~30–45 minutes.

Logs: I'll attach a short trace in the incident page (OPS-1297).

— David
VP, Serving Reliability

Subject: Status update: mitigation in progress (ETA 30–45m)

Javier / Nimble ops —

Quick update for your execs and ops crew:

- What happened: a kernel-selector rollout increased GPU memory pressure for long-context checkout requests, producing transient runtime OOMs and a spike in 5xx errors for a subset of hosts.
- What we're doing now (in-flight):
  • We paused the rollout and rebinded affected nodes to the previous kernel set.
  • We're routing long-context checkouts to the quantized 1.2.4 variant while we stabilize.
  • Added a short TTL cache for frequent cart prompts to reduce tail work.
  • Requested +2 GPU burst (awaiting infra approval).

- ETA: If the burst is approved, expected stabilization and P95 returning to baseline within ~30–45 minutes. If not approved, we expect a partial improvement within 60 minutes and full recovery within 2–3 hours as hosts drain.

Customer-facing ask: please confirm whether you want us to enable a temporary rate limiter on anonymous checkouts (low-risk) while we finish stabilization — it will reduce throughput but stop the tail failures immediately.

I'll send a short exec note for your CEO at 11:30 PT with the current status and next steps.

Attachments: nimble_slo_report.csv (original), runbook_v2.pdf (reference)

— Laura
